messages:
sam: Heads-up — hitting an odd canary routing case in prod. Requests that include header `X-Client-Tier: beta` are often landing on stable instead of the canary bucket. Repro below, and console shows 20% canary but telemetry for that header cohort is ~2%.

julia: Hmm. Was there a recent change to route evaluation order? I thought header-first matching was enabled last month.

kevin: I noticed something similar in staging yesterday. Suspect header normalization middleware is lower in the chain now, so header-based rules don't see the header in some flows.

maria: tagging @oliver-sre and @deploy-bot — can we get a policy-eval trace for one failing request? quick dump is fine.

deploy-bot: policy-eval (1749256812):
```
request: GET /v1/generate
headers: {X-Client-Tier: beta, Cookie: session=abc123}
policy-match-order: [path, weight-split, header-match]
matched-route: /v1/* -> stable
note: header-match evaluated after weight-split -> header override not applied
```

oliver-sre: that explains it — our gateway evaluates static path rules first then weight-splits, then header-specific overrides. If a request is diverted by the weight-split early, header-based explicit matches never run.

sam: Repro config we used (from the console route YAML):
```
routes:
  - match:
      path: /v1/generate
      headers:
        X-Client-Tier: beta
    action: route_canary
  - match:
      path: /v1/*
    action: route_stable
split:
  canary: 20
```

julia: So the intent was: header match should be a hard override (always go to canary if header present), then fallback to fractional split for all others. Current engine does split first which can swallow header-cohort.

kevin: Quick mitigation options: 1) flip evaluation order so header matches run before weight-split, 2) make header rules mark requests as 'pinned' so splits skip them, 3) add header-specific split keys (per-cohort split). Each has trade-offs for perf and complexity.

maria: We also need to think about telemetry and quotas. Right now console's rollout UI shows 20% canary overall, but customers relying on header override see near-zero because telemetry aggregates after the wrong evaluation. UX will be misleading.

sam: Agreed. For short term, can we add a console banner: "Note: header overrides may affect effective traffic by cohort"? Low friction. But still want engine fix.

oliver-sre: Performance note: running header matching earlier increases per-request header parsing cost for routes with many path-only fast paths. But we can short-circuit: evaluate header rules only for routes that declare them. That keeps fast path cheap.

julia: Implementation plan proposal:
- 1) Add 'override_priority' flag on route rules (default: false).
- 2) If true, route enters header-first evaluation short-circuit for that request.
- 3) Emit telemetry tag `routing.override_applied` so console shows cohort-level metrics.
This keeps default cheap and explicit for canaries that want guaranteed overrides.

kevin: I like that. Also add server-side tests for cookie-sticky scenarios — current sticky session code rehashes after split; ensure pinned header requests don't get rehashed to stable.

maria: For rollout UX, I propose console exposes two numbers: "configured split" (20%) and "effective split for header cohort" (computed from telemetry). Also surface mismatch warnings when they diverge >5%.

sam: Can we patch prod quickly with a routing rule re-order toggle so we can flip for the affected customer? We need a fast rollback if it causes perf regressions.

deploy-bot: deploy job queued — patch branch `canary-header-priority-toggle` created. Running canary on 2 nodes in us-west for 10 minutes.

oliver-sre: I'll watch latency and header-match CPU. If we see >5% p99 regression, we revert.

julia: Post-mortem items: add unit test for policy-eval order, add integration test for header override + sticky cookie, add telemetry tag and console warning. Assigning follow-ups:
- kevin: engine change + tests
- oliver-sre: perf guard and rollout monitor
- maria: console banner and split mismatch UI

sam: Thanks. One last ask — can we have a small docs blurb in rollout UX about "cohort overrides" so PMs know header-based canaries are guaranteed unless you opt into fractional-first behavior.

maria: Yup, I'll draft a quick blurb and link it from the canary config screen.

kevin: I'll open the PR for the flag and include the policy-eval logs in the tests. ETA EOD tomorrow.

sam: Great. Leaving this thread open for the rollout watch. Please ping if any telemetry shows more than 10% divergence. :eyes:
